display.title: Bubby Chaya Malka's Yiddish Stories, Part 2
display.summary_short: The grandmother's stories continue in Yiddish: Shmuel HaNavi hears Hashem's call, Eliyahu HaNavi's blessed coin, and the family cup that brought Eliyahu to a poor family's Seder.
display.summary_long: Second half of Bubby Chaya Malka's home recording of Yiddish stories for her grandchildren before Pesach. It opens in the middle of the story of Shmuel HaNavi: the boy serves Eli HaKohen in the Beis HaMikdash, hears his name called three times at night, and learns to answer 'Hineni', becoming a navi who will anoint the next king. Next, Eliyahu HaNavi offers an honest field worker seven good years. His wise wife chooses to have them now, records every mitzvah she does with the blessed coin in a big book, and when Eliyahu returns he lets them keep the coin. The last story tells of a once-rich family with nothing for Pesach. The wife refuses to sell the precious cup handed down in her family for generations. An old man visits, gives her two dollars, and the money keeps coming back to her pocket until the house is ready for Yom Tov. At the Seder Eliyahu HaNavi comes, and he blesses the home because the mother protected his cup.
display.lesson: Use Hashem's blessings for mitzvos, trust that He will provide, and treasure what is holy rather than giving it up.

advisories.note: A family loses everything and has nothing for Pesach; the father storms out in despair before Eliyahu HaNavi helps them.
